# Nautical Examination Marshals Office Standard Operating Procedure
These are sets of regulations and polices used by NEMO for their operations and sqauds, plus deployment criteria for NEMO personnel.
\nNEMO personnel Failing to follow the Standard Operating Procedure may result in capital Class-X charges under the authority of the Marshal Intelligence Service. Military personnel failing to follow procedures in contacting NEMO assets may be charged at the discretion of Marshal Intervention Group.
## What is NEMO?
The Nautical Examination Marshal's Office, or NEMO for short, serves as the highest authority on military law, police oversight, and judicial compliance throughout the frontier worlds.
Founded following a series of high-profile mutinies, unlawful detentions, and command abuses during the expansion into frontier space, NEMO was granted extraordinary authority to oversee all Military Police and ensure uniform enforcement of the Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ), and the enforcement of international law and policies. While Military Police answer to their local commands, NEMO answers only to its own chain of authority and the government that chartered it.
NEMO Personnel possess the authority to review arrests, investigate misconduct, overturn unlawful rulings, and intervene in matters concerning military justice. Their rulings supersede those of local Military Police and, in matters of law, may even overrule Commanding Officers, it has been reported that NEMO has even granted itself exemptions from UCMJ in order to conduct its duty.
## NEMO Teams and Sqauds To support its mission, NEMO maintains several specialized divisions, reportedly its for checks and balances on the military justice system, and to ensure it can operate effectively across the frontier. These teams include:
• The Special Enforcement Detachment (SED) investigates allegations of injustice, corruption, unlawful punishment, and criminal appeals.
• The Marshal Intervention Group (MIG) executes arrests, detentions, and enforcement actions resulting from NEMO investigations.
• The Marshal Intelligence Service (MIS) conducts covert surveillance, intelligence gathering, infiltration, and evidence collection operations.
• The Instability Response Group (IRG) deploys during riots, mutinies, and internal security incidents, restoring order through measured force and non-lethal intervention.
• The Civil Protection Insurrection Stability & Protection Force (CPISP) serves as NEMO's premier tactical unit, protecting senior officials and responding to severe threats against government authority.
• The Marshal Orbital Response Wing (MORW) provides aerospace transportation, extraction, prisoner transfer, and rapid deployment capabilities for NEMO operations across the frontier.
To most marines, NEMO is rarely seen and often unwelcome. Its arrival usually signifies that something has gone terribly wrong. Whether investigating a wrongful execution, suppressing a Military Police rebellion, or escorting a high-value prisoner off-world, NEMO represents the final authority of military law.
Among people covered by NEMO, one saying remains common:
"When NEMO arrives, the investigation is already over. They're just here to decide who pays for it."
